artifacts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: top-down aerial bomb game icon for Age of Fronts, WWII-era aircraft payload, one individual bomb, square transparent PNG, final 627 x 627 pixels.
Input image 1 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match the realistic hand-painted game asset finish, muted olive and grey metal, readable overhead geometry, weathered surface grain and subtle lighting. No factory, buildings, weapons bench, crates or environment.
Primary request: a single conventional WWII-style aerial bomb that would be dropped from a bomber, seen directly from above with its full longitudinal body silhouette visible.
Composition: true orthographic overhead plan view, bomb lying horizontally in the imaginary image plane, length oriented vertically on the canvas with rounded streamlined nose at the top and tail fins at the bottom. The imaginary support surface is absent. One complete centered bomb fills about 80 percent of the canvas height, with generous clear transparent margins, clean readable silhouette.
Subject and details: one olive-drab steel aerial bomb, tapered rounded ogive nose, robust cylindrical middle body narrowing to a finned tail. Conventional symmetrical steel cruciform stabilizing tail fin assembly, with correct straight-above projection: the horizontal pair spreads left and right and the vertical fin is a thin central ridge. Tidy coherent manufacture, visible panel seams, lightly worn painted metal edges and discreet yellow identification band. No readable codes, words, numbering or labels.
Style: polished realistic hand-painted 2D strategy-game sprite, moderate tactile surface detail and restrained highlights that read well at small size, same material realism as the reference assets.
Constraints: only ONE bomb, no explosion, fire, sparks, falling trail, airplane, detached ground shadow, display pedestal, ground tile or environmental scenery. No text, logo, watermark or schematic cutaway. No isometric view, perspective tilt or large visible side elevation. Genuinely transparent alpha outside the bomb silhouette, never a white or checkerboard painted background.
